newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt raises rubber intervention price.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt raises rubber intervention price.

text.p: The Thai government on Friday succumbed to rubber producers' demands and agreed to raise its intervention price for grade-3 sheet rubber to 29.00 baht a kg from 27.50 baht previously, an official in southern Trang province said on Friday.

The move came after thousands of rubber tappers in Trang and other major rubber-producing provinces in the south held a protest and demanded that the government buy rubber from them at 30-35 baht per kg as world rubber prices slide.
Deputy agricultural minister Krish Kongpetchara personally negotiated with the tappers, the official said.
"They finally agreed at 29 baht. The government will earmark 4.4 billion baht for this intervention scheme. However, the plan must be approved by the cabinet before it will take effect," he said.
This is the second time this year the government has raised the minimum guaranteed prices to help the local rubber industry amid a bearish global rubber market.
The government is expected to start buying at the new price from May 13, the official said.
